title: Shared-memory bank thrashing in interleaved attention kernels — Nsight captures & mitigation experiments
content:
Summary:
We ran a targeted Nsight investigation for an interleaved attention kernel variant used by the microbatch-path (packing multiple short sequences into a single CUDA Graph replay). Captures show recurrent SM idle gaps and sudden drops in achieved active warps that align with bursts of shared-memory bank conflict stalls. This doc collects observations, lightweight reproducer commands, measured telemetry, and next-step mitigations to validate.

Background / why this matters:
- Workload: many short sequences (len 8–64) aggregated into a microbatch; kernel implements tiled attention with per-threadblock shared-memory buffering and an index remapping to handle variable lengths.
- Symptom: despite moderate occupancy (40–70%), tail latency spikes and throughput regressions appear when sequence-length distribution is skewed (lots of short + some medium).
- Hypothesis: the per-TB index remapping and interleaved loads produce correlated shared-memory bank access patterns across warps, causing bank thrashing and serialization that reduces instruction issue efficiency and produces SM idle periods.

Environment & capture setup:
- HW: A100 40GB (DGX-style node, single card pinned).
- Driver/CUDA: 525.105.17 / CUDA 12.1.
- Build: serving-runtime@release-2026-05 + local patch to switch to interleaved-attn-v2 kernel. Commit: a1b2c3d (PR linked).
- Nsight settings: API tracing OFF, Timeline capture mode, All CUDA activity, Samples: 1s warmup + 2s capture; Timestamp resolution 1us.
- Capture knobs: enable L2 and shared-memory counters, per-SM warp occupancy, issue efficiency, and warp stall reasons.

Lightweight reproducer (local):
1) Start runtime with --microbatch-packing=enabled --pack-threshold=64
2) Run workload generator (short-heavy distribution):
   python tools/loadgen.py --seq-dist short-heavy --concurrency 48 --tokens/second 12000 --duration 60
3) In parallel: nv-nsight-cu-cli --metrics sm__warps_active.avg,sm__issue_active.avg,sm__pipe_fp16.active_cycles,sm__pipe_utilization.avg,sys__shared_store_transactions_per_request.avg --target-processes all --section "Launches" --output capture.ncu-rep ./serving-runtime-binary

Key observations from captures (selected snippets):
- Timeline: periodic bursts (~70–110ms cadence) where "issued warps" drops by ~25–40% and SM idle jumps from ~12% to 45% across majority of SMs. Those bursts line up with a specific kernel-id: interleaved_attn_v2_kernel_main (approx 1.2–1.6ms launches).
- Warp-level stats: in bursts, 'warp_stalled_membar' and 'warp_stalled_mem_pipe' increase modestly, but the dominant stall reason increases is 'warp_stalled_inst_retry' and 'warp_stalled_other' (which correlates with bank conflict internal stalls per offline analysis).
- Shared-memory metrics: shared_store_transactions_per_request increases by ~3x within bursts; bank-conflict proxy (divergent access pattern sampling) shows spikes localized to specific threadblock offsets.
- L2 & DRAM: no corresponding increase in DRAM bandwidth; L2 hit rate slightly decreases (<4%), so this is not a DRAM bottleneck.
- CUDA Graph behavior: when replaying a captured graph, bursts are more pronounced — likely because deterministic launch order makes the interleaved indices align across multiple TBs compared to JIT/non-graph where scheduler noise masks the alignment.

Microtrace example (compressed):
- t=1250ms: interleaved_attn_v2_kernel_main launch (grid 512, block 256)
- t=1251.4ms: shared-store tx per request = 0.48 -> 1.6
- t=1251.45ms: per-SM active warps drop 27%
- t=1252.6ms: kernel complete; SM idle reduces back to baseline

Repro experiments we ran and results:
1) Pad shared-memory tiles (add +8 bytes per slot): slight reduction in peak bank transactions (-12%), small throughput improvement (+3%), tail P99 improved ~6%.
2) Rotate warp-to-bank mapping (thread indexing remap): large reduction in bank collision proxy (-55%), throughput +12%, issue efficiency +9%. Caveat: increased register pressure by ~2 regs/TB.
3) Stagger kernel launch by micro-sleep (host-side usleep(50–200us) between graph submissions): reduces alignment and shrinks bursts but increases average latency (because of serialized submissions). Not acceptable for high-throughput mode.
4) Change block-size from 256->192 (more TBs in flight): occupancy drops slightly but throughput increases modestly (+4%) and bank spikes diminish. Suggests different scheduling across SMs breaks bad alignment.
5) Convert shared loads to use vectorized 128-bit transactions where possible: measurable reduction in store transactions and improved issue efficiency but requires refactor in the tiled load path.

Interpretation & root cause (working theory):
- The index-remap / interleaving pattern causes multiple TBs to access shared-memory addresses that map to the same banks at near-identical times. When many TBs launch in lockstep (common in CUDA Graph replay), these accesses line up and create bank serialization (internal bank conflicts) that shows up as increased shared-store transactions per request and immediate warp stalls, even when occupancy would otherwise be adequate.
- Non-DRAM metrics confirm this is internal shared-memory contention (not memory bandwidth bound).

Short-term mitigations (safe to try in-prod canary):
- Deploy padding patch (adds 4–8 bytes pad per shared tile) — low-risk; recompile kernels as fallbackable artifact; run canary at 5% traffic. Linked PR includes compile-time guard.
- Disable strictly deterministic microbatch packing for customers on Dedicated until we ship robust fix (config flag --pack-alignment=relaxed). Operational cost: slightly higher per-token overhead.

Medium-term fixes (engineering work):
- Implement warp-bank remapping option in kernel (rotation based on TB id) — requires register pressure analysis and microbenching across model families.
- Add optional runtime jitter to kernel launch ordering inside CUDA Graph replay executor (small intentional desync to avoid pathological alignment) — must be gated behind perf flag.
- Consider persistent-kernel variant that serializes interleaving in-kernel (scheduling internal micro-queues) to avoid cross-TB bank collisions; significant refactor but could yield large gains for short-seq workloads.

Experiment plan & acceptance criteria:
- Phase A (1 week): land padding + pack-alignment=relaxed flag; run 72h A/B on staging trace; acceptance: P99 tail latency reduction >= 5% without >2% regression in avg throughput.
- Phase B (2–3 weeks): prototype bank-rotation mapping; microbench across seq-lens; target throughput +10% vs baseline for short-heavy workload.
- Phase C (quarter): evaluate persistent-kernel approach for sustained short-seq microbatch throughput; success = throughput >= current best with 20% lower tail.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need a deterministic microtrace generator that reproduces worst-case bank alignment in unit tests (Samira to produce seeded generator).
- Measure impact of increased register use from rotation on occupancy across other models (Ethan to run regression on decoder-only 20B).
- Check interaction with LRU-based KV cache spilling (could change TB alignment patterns) — link with infra team to get production capture for a customer trace (Miguel).

Attachments referenced inside capture notes:
- nsight capture: gs://redwood-dev-captures/sharedmem-thrash-20260612.nsys (redacted access)
- sample trace csv (perf counters): gs://redwood-dev-captures/sharedmem-thrash-counters-20260612.csv

Conclusions (current):
- Evidence strongly points to shared-memory bank serialization due to aligned interleaved access across many TBs, amplified by CUDA Graph replay determinism. Simple padding and warp-bank rotation show most promise; persistent-kernel is a larger investment but likely most robust.

Recommended immediate actions:
1) Ship padding patch behind feature flag and enable canary. (Owner: Aisha)
2) Start prototyping warp rotation mapping; measure register pressure tradeoffs. (Owner: Samira)
3) Create deterministic unit generator for bank-alignment tests. (Owner: Miguel)

Notes-to-self / scratch ideas:
- Could try a compile-time parameter for bank stride that depends on model tile size.
- Investigate whether compiler-level shared memory layout pragmas (cuda __attribute__ hacks) useful across GCC/Clang builds.
- Keep an eye on NUMA/GPU topology effects for multi-GPU runs; alignment may change with different bus topologies.

If you want to reproduce quickly: ping me for the lightweight capture script and I can drop a focused docker with our patched kernel and the loadgen config.
